1.explanation: All of the layout and data-ordering logic for List lives in List.js. The List component itself renders each item’s content, ordering controls, and the action button. The helper function normalize builds the per-item properties object (including action and order controls) and reorder merges the pinned and orderable data when onOrder is provided. Because the misalignment only occurs when onOrder is used alongside action, the rendering logic in List (and its normalize and reorder helpers) must be updated to wrap and style the action and order controls together so the action button remains right-aligned even when ordering controls are present.
1.bug_scenario: When a List is rendered with both an action button and onOrder enabled, the action button no longer stays right-aligned next to each item. Instead it stretches across the full width of the list row and the up/down order controls float separately, causing misalignment. Without onOrder the action button correctly sits at the far right of its item.

2.explanation: The List component itself is responsible for composing each row, choosing whether to show ordering controls (when onOrder is provided) or a standalone action. The normalize function shapes the raw item data (including the action slot) for rendering but does not account for reserving space when ordering controls are present. The reorder function injects the up/down buttons into the item layout, which shifts or replaces the normal action column. Because normalize and reorder do not coordinate the action cell’s placement when onOrder is active, the action Button gets rendered in the wrong column or stretched. Fixing the alignment requires updating normalize (and/or the List render logic) to include the action cell in the final row structure even when reorder has inserted ordering controls.
2.bug_scenario: When a Grommet List is given both an action and an onOrder handler, the action Button no longer lines up on the right edge of each list item. Instead, as soon as onOrder is present the Button stretches to full width (or is placed into the ordering control column) and the up/down arrows take over the normal content layout, resulting in the misalignment shown in the “with onOrder” screenshot, whereas without onOrder the action Button is correctly right-aligned.
